JFRK.title: This knight can jump to any empty square. Where should it land? #shorts
JFRK.desc:
In Joker Chess each player gets one jump per game: a queen, rook, bishop or knight goes to any empty square, but it can't capture or give check. Here the knight jumps from b1 to d6 and hits the queen on b7 and the rook on e8 at once; after ...Qc7 it takes the rook.

Did you find d6?

JBEA.title: How do you beat a Joker in chess? #shorts
JBEA.desc:
In fairy chess the Joker is a real piece: it moves like the last piece the other side moved. Black plays a knight, and the Joker jumps like a knight; Black plays the queen, and it moves like a queen. So keep moving pawns, and it can only move like a pawn. It's a chess variant, like Fischer random chess. In Joker Chess, a newer variant, the Joker isn't a piece at all: it's one jump per game to any empty square.

Which Joker would you rather play against?
